name: Record and interpret local weather
description: Measure the weather where you are, record it, and compare it with a forecast without treating the forecast as your own observation.
emoji_rationale: The sun behind a cloud stands for weather you observe and record.

levels.name: Measure and record
levels.completion_criterion: Take one weather measurement you can explain, such as temperature or rainfall, and record the place and time.
levels.can_do: You can show a measurement and how you took it.
levels.safety_requirements: Use the instrument only as its own instructions allow. Do not invent a medical or storm-safety procedure.

levels.name: Relate several signs
levels.completion_criterion: At one time, record more than one kind of sign, such as cloud and wind or temperature and rain, and say how they fit the conditions you see.
levels.can_do: You can connect the readings to the scene.
levels.safety_requirements: A badge timetable is not the progression. The Scout page's two-week rule is not copied as a level.

levels.name: Compare with a forecast
levels.completion_criterion: Compare your record with a published forecast and state one agreement and one difference, including fronts or isobars only if you can point to them on the map you used.
levels.can_do: You can separate your observation from the forecast.
levels.safety_requirements: Do not claim a forecast you cannot show.

safety_notes: Pilot only. Not a severe-weather safety course.

name: Explain how a visual communicates
description: Explain how an image and any text together make a point, instead of only describing what the picture shows.
emoji_rationale: The eye stands for looking at how a visual makes its point.

levels.name: State the point
levels.completion_criterion: For one visual document, say what it is mainly trying to communicate.
levels.can_do: You can separate the message from a list of objects in the picture.
levels.safety_requirements: The Purdue page does not require a judgement for or against the piece.

levels.name: Point to choices
levels.completion_criterion: Identify visible choices, such as an image, the layout, or the words, and say what each one does.
levels.can_do: You can talk about choices rather than only retell the picture.
levels.safety_requirements: Do not invent the designer's private intention.

levels.name: Explain the strategy
levels.completion_criterion: Explain how those choices support or weaken the message, and mark one thing you cannot tell from the document alone.
levels.can_do: You can give a reading of the visual and its limit.
levels.safety_requirements: This is not a lesson in making the graphic.

name: Sketch what you see in the sky
description: Draw an astronomical object while you are looking at it, and correct the drawing from a second look rather than from a photograph.
emoji_rationale: The pen stands for a sketch made while looking, not a processed photo.

levels.name: Sketch while looking
levels.completion_criterion: Draw one object you are looking at and mark which direction is which.
levels.can_do: You can make a sketch from the view, not from a photo.
levels.safety_requirements: Do not sketch the Sun. Solar observing is outside this proposal.

levels.name: Record the view
levels.completion_criterion: Add the place, the time, and whether you used your eyes, binoculars, or a telescope, plus one detail you noticed only by looking longer.
levels.can_do: You can connect the drawing to the conditions.
levels.safety_requirements: The League's award count is not the level criterion.

levels.name: Correct from a second look
levels.completion_criterion: Look again and change one mark that was not actually visible. Leave the correction visible.
levels.can_do: You can revise the sketch against the sky.
levels.safety_requirements: Do not add detail from a photograph.

safety_notes: Pilot only. Do not observe the Sun.

name: Play xiangqi
description: Play a game of xiangqi whose aim is the opponent's general, using a reference for the setup and the moves rather than a memorised rule book in this proposal.
emoji_rationale: The pawn marks a board game with a different aim and setup from the chess already familiar to many players.

levels.name: Set up from a reference
levels.completion_criterion: Set the starting position from a diagram you can show, including the river and the palaces.
levels.can_do: You can set up a game.
levels.safety_requirements: Move rules are not copied into these levels. Use a reference when you are unsure.

levels.name: Finish a game
levels.completion_criterion: Play until the opponent's general is checkmated or a player has no legal move, and say which of those ended it.
levels.can_do: You can finish a game for the stated aim.
levels.safety_requirements: The cited page says stalemate is a win for the player who delivers it. Do not treat it as a draw.

levels.name: Review one position
levels.completion_criterion: After the game, point to one position where a piece was left open and say what you would do differently.
levels.can_do: You can learn from a position you actually reached.
levels.safety_requirements: This is not a coaching certificate and not a federation syllabus.

safety_notes: Pilot only. Not a federation course. Confidence: medium.
